consumer_seed: The Ofcom vulnerable-people page was published on 30 November 2022.
Ofcom states that vulnerability can be temporary or permanent.
UK communications providers must have clear and effective policies and procedures for identifying customers in vulnerable circumstances.
Required services for disabled customers include priority fault repair, text relay and free directory enquiries.
Deaf British Sign Language users can access a free video relay service for contacting the emergency services.
Since December 2021, customers who need an accessible format because of disability can receive communications-service information in formats such as braille or large print.
The Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide was published on 13 October 2023.
The Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide was last updated on 8 April 2026.
Telephone extension leads can cause interference that lowers broadband speed.
Microfilters should be plugged into every phone socket used in the home where applicable.
Electrical and wireless devices can affect routers, so Ofcom advises keeping the router away from them.
A phone or broadband service bought online or by phone can generally be cancelled up to 14 days after entering the contract.
A provider may be able to detect a technical problem by accessing the router remotely.
Connecting a computer directly with an Ethernet cable can help establish whether there is a line fault.
The Ofcom codes-of-practice page was published on 28 April 2010.
The Ofcom codes-of-practice page was last updated on 16 July 2025.
The updated broadband speeds codes apply to broadband purchases from 21 December 2022.
General Condition C4 is the relevant condition for complaints handling and dispute resolution.
Under General Condition C4.2, providers must follow procedures conforming to the Ofcom Approved Complaints Code for domestic and small-business complaints.
Under General Condition C4.3, providers must belong to and comply with an approved ADR scheme.
Ofcom may impose a penalty of up to ten per cent of turnover for failure to comply with a formal notification within the specified period.
From 1 April 2019, participating broadband and home-phone providers introduced compensation for delayed repairs, missed engineer appointments and delayed service starts.
The Ofcom changing-provider problem guide was published on 24 July 2023.
The Ofcom changing-provider problem guide was last updated on 8 April 2026.
A customer switched without consent should contact the old provider and ask to be switched back as soon as possible.
A customer switched without consent should also tell the provider that took over the service that the switch was not agreed.
An attempted unauthorised switch should be cancelled through the current provider, which should be possible up to 24 hours before the scheduled switch.
An unresolved switching complaint can be escalated by requesting a deadlock letter from the provider.
After six weeks from the first formal complaint, a customer can contact the relevant ADR scheme directly.
Ofcom identifies CISAS and Communications Ombudsman as the two telecoms ADR schemes, and providers must belong to one of them.
expansion_rule: For each BDUK contract emit ten records: January supplier, January contracted, January built or explicit missing guard, February contracted, February built, contracted delta, built delta or missing guard, built percentage change or missing/zero-base guard, January built share or missing guard, and February built share. Append 30 Ofcom records. Every fifth expanded record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
